_help: Latest in AI. Newest first. Every item: date (official publish date), category, company (tile colour/monogram), impact (major|notable|minor = importance, see _impact_rule), plain headline, 1-2 sentence beginner explainer (first sentence = one-line 'For you'), source_url (official announcement or reputable outlet you actually opened). Optional x: the announcing post (kind official) or most-engaged credible post about it (kind coverage), real likes/reposts/views + posted_at + measured_at; no post found = no x block. Heat/top story/trending are computed in build.py. If an item changes model prices, update data/ai-pricing.json too.

items.headline: Gemini API now saves requests by default for new paid projects
items.explainer: If you set up a new paid Gemini API project, the prompts your bot sends are now stored by default, matching Google's Interactions API; existing projects don't change. If you'd rather they weren't kept, send store=false or turn off Generate Content API logging under Logs and Datasets.

items.headline: Kimi K3.1 Pro: a new open model that says it nearly matches Claude Opus 5.5 at coding
items.explainer: Moonshot's new Kimi K3.1 Pro is out now in the Kimi apps and API, and its full weights are due by Nov 4, so anyone will be able to download and run it. Its API price is $2 in / $10 out per million tokens, half of Claude Opus 5.5's list price; the coding scores are Moonshot's own and haven't been checked independently yet.

items.headline: Cursor's coding bot can now click and type in other apps on your computer
items.explainer: After you update the Cursor app, its agent can drive desktop apps such as the iPhone simulator to test the features it just built, instead of you tapping through them yourself. Because it works by looking at your screen, close private windows before you let it take over.

items.headline: NVIDIA releases a free 4GB AI model for assistants that run on your own device
items.explainer: Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B is a small, free open model built for fast local voice and device assistants that can follow instructions and use tools, so a simple bot can run on your own computer with no per-message bill. It's text-only with a 64K-token memory, so save bigger jobs for the large cloud models.

items.headline: Block shows Dessa, a voice AI that talks with human-like pauses and emotion
items.explainer: Dessa is a speech model from the company behind Square and Cash App that listens and talks at the same time, so conversations with it sound strikingly like a real person. There's no public access yet, only early access for safety researchers, but it's a reminder that a lifelike voice on the phone may not be a person.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts its newest models off the live internet while they're being trained
items.explainer: OpenAI says its frontier models now train in an offline copy of the web instead of the real internet, a safety step so a model in training can't reach outside systems. Nothing changes in ChatGPT for you, but it shows labs are treating stronger models as something to keep fenced in.

items.headline: OpenAI's Agents API can now run bots on a schedule
items.explainer: Developers can now tell an OpenAI agent to run on a repeating schedule, like every morning at 10, or once at a set time, and the agent can even set up its own schedules when you ask in plain words. Expect more apps that do a recurring job for you, such as a daily digest, without you opening them.

items.headline: OpenAI switched off older models including GPT-4, GPT-3.5 Turbo, o4-mini and gpt-image-1
items.explainer: If an older app or bot of yours suddenly stopped working on Oct 23, this may be why: OpenAI retired a batch of older models announced back in April. Switching it to a current model such as GPT-5.6 usually fixes it.

items.headline: Anthropic hands Agent Skills to a neutral foundation
items.explainer: Skills are little instruction folders that teach an AI agent a specific task, and more than 70 tools, including ChatGPT, Cursor and GitHub Copilot, already read them. Moving the standard to the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation makes it more likely a skill you set up once keeps working across different bots.

items.headline: OpenAI's quick-answer Decisions API is now open to all developers
items.explainer: The Decisions API turns text or images into short typed answers, like sorting an email or approving a request, without writing a full reply, and it now handles up to 400 questions per request with prompt-cache discounts. Apps built on it can make these small calls faster and cheaper, which adds up for bots that triage a lot.

items.headline: Canva launches Craft, its own image model built for designs with readable text
items.explainer: Craft plans the layout first, then makes images up to 2K in about 30 sizes, and is trained on human-made Canva templates so text comes out legible. It's available to all Canva users in the Dream Lab tab, and Canva plans to let ChatGPT and Gemini use it too.

items.headline: Claude will stop asking permission for every step, starting next week
items.explainer: Starting next week, Claude's web, desktop and mobile apps on Pro, Max and Team plans begin sessions in auto mode, where an automated check lets safe actions go ahead and blocks risky ones instead of asking you to approve each step. Longer tasks finish with fewer interruptions, and you can switch any session back to manual approvals.

items.headline: Grok Bot can now use your phone's Calendar, Reminders and Contacts
items.explainer: With your permission, Grok Bot on iOS and Android can add calendar events, set and check reminders, look up contacts and reach apps like Messages and Home, and you allow each app separately. That makes "add this to my calendar" or "remind me tonight" something you can just ask your bot to do; it's rolling out now.

items.headline: Grok Bot can sign in to your accounts with 1Password, without seeing your passwords
items.explainer: You approve which saved logins your bot may use, and 1Password fills them in, one-time codes included, so the bot never sees the password. 1Password says the same approach is rolling out for Meta's Muse and coming soon to Claude Duet and ChatGPT Work, at no extra cost on its Individual and Family plans.

items.headline: Gemini can now plan your day from your Google Maps saved places and calendar
items.explainer: If you turn on Personal Intelligence, Gemini can check your Maps searches and saved places alongside your Calendar, so "which restaurant on my list is near my last meeting?" gets a real answer. Google is also telling AI Ultra subscribers that Gemini 4 Argon will soon replace the Deep Think mode.

items.headline: Anthropic opens Claude Duet, a proactive agent that comes to you
items.explainer: Claude Duet sends you a morning brief from your connected apps, keeps an eye on them through the day, works on tasks while you're away, and asks before it does anything big like paying or deleting. It's a waitlist research preview for US Pro and Max subscribers, on iOS, Android and claude.ai, and Anthropic says it can still misjudge what's urgent.

items.headline: AI agents helped find critical PHP flaws that affect most websites
items.explainer: If you run a website or blog on PHP (WordPress included), make sure your host has updated PHP to the patched version now. OpenAI says its models helped researchers find the bugs before attackers did, and it's sharing a version checker and a Codex skill to help site owners check.

items.headline: Claude Security now re-scans your code every time it changes
items.explainer: Teams on Claude Enterprise can connect their code once and Claude keeps checking new changes for security holes, marking each one fixed when the fix lands. It's a public beta for businesses, not something personal plans get.

items.headline: OpenAI's models are coming to Google Cloud
items.explainer: Companies on Google Cloud will be able to use GPT-6 models and Codex without a separate OpenAI account (private preview now, wider launch planned in the coming weeks). For you it mostly means more places your work tools can quietly plug in OpenAI models.

items.headline: Recursive releases Flint, a free coding model that runs on a laptop
items.explainer: Flint is a free, open coding model small enough to run on an ordinary laptop, so a coding bot can work offline, keep your files private and skip per-use fees. Its maker says it still needs smaller, step-by-step tasks than the big paid assistants.

items.headline: Mistral launches Voxtral 3 for voice agents that can take calls
items.explainer: A new set of speech models plus a kit for building phone and web voice agents that listen, look things up and talk back in 50+ languages. Mistral lists its voice agent API at $0.04 a minute with Mistral Small 4, so phone bots keep getting cheaper to run.

items.headline: OpenAI adds 12-hour prompt caching
items.explainer: Bots that run hours apart (like a morning and an evening check) can now keep their fixed instructions cached and pay the lower cached-input price. Writing to the 12-hour cache costs 2.5x the normal input price, so it pays off when the same setup is reused several times.

items.headline: DeepSeek open-sources the engine that runs its own API
items.explainer: DeepInfer is the software DeepSeek uses to serve V4.1 Flash cheaply, now free under Apache 2.0. Hosting companies can copy the tricks, which could push the price of running open models down for your bots.

items.headline: Meta pauses Muse chat sharing after shared chats turned up on the web
items.explainer: Researchers found more than 6,800 Muse share links through public web records, some showing loan applications, revenue reviews and work calendars, so Meta switched sharing off while it reviews. Treat any AI "share link" as public, and keep private details out of chats you share.

items.headline: Gemini in your car can now use your Gmail, Calendar and Maps to help
items.explainer: With your permission, Gemini on Android Auto can pull your flight gate from email, find the restaurant you saved, or take you to your next appointment without you looking anything up. It's rolling out now on Android Auto for eligible personal accounts and is off until you turn it on.

items.headline: ChatGPT lets you lock private chats behind a PIN
items.explainer: You can now lock a sensitive ChatGPT chat from its ••• menu so it's hidden from your history and search and opens only with a 4-digit PIN or your phone's face or fingerprint unlock. Write the PIN down, because resetting a forgotten one deletes every locked chat for good; it's rolling out gradually.

more_sources.label: OpenAI Help Center: Using locked chats

items.headline: Google turns Gemini Gems into Skills and moves Spark into the main chat
items.explainer: From November 17, Google starts converting personal Gems into Skills you call with a slash in the main chat, and Scheduled Actions no longer need a paid plan (still rolling out to free accounts). If you built a Gem-based bot, test it before the switch.

items.headline: DeepSeek updates its V4.1 Flash model: faster and shorter answers, same price
items.explainer: DeepSeek says the update finishes tasks faster with shorter outputs, which means fewer tokens to pay for. The API name and prices are unchanged, and the open weights are on Hugging Face.

items.headline: DeepSeek opens its own web search and page-fetch tools to developers
items.explainer: Bots built on DeepSeek can now search the web and read pages through DeepSeek's own API at $0.75 per 1,000 requests each. Calls made through some coding agents are free until billing starts on November 1 (Beijing time).

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Spark Open, the most capable US open-weight model so far
items.explainer: Meta's new open model is built for coding and agent work, and you can call it on day one through Groq, OpenRouter, Together AI and other APIs. Groq runs it at 350+ tokens per second per user. That speed matters for agents, because each task is a long chain of model calls.

items.headline: xAI releases Grok Voice 3.0, its new speech-to-speech model
items.explainer: The voice model behind Grok Bot's voice mode and Tesla's in-car assistant got an upgrade, at the same $0.08 a minute on the API. xAI says it answers in under a second and handles interruptions, which is what makes a phone bot feel natural.

items.headline: Google's Gemini 4 Argon is now available to developers and paid Gemini users
items.explainer: Google's new top model is in the API at an introductory $2 / $10 per million tokens, and in the Gemini app for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Google built it for long, multi-step work, the kind agents do.

items.headline: Meta releases Muse Wonder, its first frontier model
items.explainer: Meta says Muse Wonder will soon power its Muse personal agent, starting with paying subscribers. Developers can use it through Meta's API at $4 / $20 per million tokens.

items.headline: Gemini's Spark agent moves to a "Task" button on the app's home screen
items.explainer: Handing a job to Google's background agent is now one tap away in the Gemini app, with a new Scheduled page that shows active, paused and finished tasks. It's live on Android and iOS; web wasn't confirmed yet.

items.headline: OpenAI stops charging agents for idle sandbox time
items.explainer: Agents built on OpenAI's Agents API run in a hosted sandbox computer, and that is now billed only during active turns, not while the agent waits for you. Sandboxes can also be pre-warmed so replies start faster.

items.headline: Claude can now build live dashboards from your data and animated explainers
items.explainer: Ask a question in plain words and Claude builds a dashboard that stays current, showing the query behind every number. Motion turns a report into a short animation you can export as MP4. Both are in beta on paid plans (Motion on Team and Enterprise).

items.headline: GPT-6 rolls out to everyone in ChatGPT, with interactive answers
items.explainer: ChatGPT answers can now include charts, buttons, forms and small tools you use right in the chat. Paid plans get GPT-6 Sol and Free and Go users get GPT-6 Luna, starting October 8.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5, a fast, cheap model for high-volume bot work
items.explainer: At $0.10 / $0.50 per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens, Anthropic says it costs about 75% less to run than Haiku 4.5. It's built for summaries, sorting and browser use: the simple, repeated jobs most everyday bots do.

items.headline: Anthropic halves Sonnet 5.5 cache reads and gives Max and Team plans monthly API credits
items.explainer: Cached reads on Claude Sonnet 5.5 dropped from $0.20 to $0.10 per million tokens, which Anthropic says makes most agent work about 20% cheaper. Max subscribers get $100 or $200 a month in API credits, and Team plans up to $500, to build their own bots.

items.headline: Mistral previews Mistral Large 4, with open weights promised by month's end
items.explainer: Mistral's biggest model yet is in a public preview on its API, and Mistral says anyone will be able to download and run it themselves later this month. That's good news if you want a strong model you can host privately.

items.headline: Claude now works inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides
items.explainer: A Claude sidebar can read the file you have open and edit it in place, asking before each change by default. It's in beta on all paid Claude plans, so your doc-and-spreadsheet chores can go to Claude without copy-pasting.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Sol: near-top performance at a fifth of the price
items.explainer: OpenAI says GPT-6.1 Sol nearly matches its top model, GPT-6 Astra, on agent work at one-fifth of Astra's token prices ($2 / $10 per million). For bot builders, it's a cheaper middle option for jobs a small model can't handle.

items.headline: OpenAI's Agents API can now use a web browser
items.explainer: Agents built on OpenAI's platform can now complete tasks in an OpenAI-hosted browser, with the app asking you before it visits a site and handling sign-in. Expect more third-party bots that click through websites for you.

items.headline: OpenAI launches dots: always-on agents with their own computer
items.explainer: A dot runs on GPT-6 Astra with its own cloud computer, connects to your apps, and keeps working between chats, checking with you on decisions. It's rolling out to ChatGPT Pro and Business Premium users first (not the EU, Switzerland or the UK on Pro at launch).

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Sonnet 5.5
items.explainer: Anthropic says Sonnet 5.5 runs 30%+ faster than Sonnet 5 and costs up to 30% less for most work. It's the middle model many agent apps use by default.

items.headline: Grok Bot adds Team Bots: shared AI teammates for a whole team
items.explainer: One person sets up a bot with the files, apps and skills it needs, then the whole team can use it in Slack or Grok Bot, while each person's chats stay private. It's in public beta for Teams and Enterprise plans.

items.headline: Anthropic releases Claude Opus 5.5
items.explainer: Anthropic says Opus 5.5 leads in agentic coding and knowledge work and costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads. It's the model to reach for when a bot's job is hard, not routine.

items.headline: OpenAI releases GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna
items.explainer: Two new models: Sol for most work and Luna, a very cheap one at $0.10 / $0.50 per million tokens. Luna is the kind of model to use for simple, frequent bot jobs.

items.headline: xAI releases Grok 4.7
items.explainer: xAI's new model for coding and knowledge work keeps the same $2 / $6 per million token price as Grok 4.6. xAI says it was trained to work inside the Grok Bot harness, which should make Grok Bot better at everyday tasks.

_impact_rule: Importance, not popularity. major = a new flagship model or a major agent launch from a big lab (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta, xAI). minor = small changelog-level tweaks (a billing detail, a new tool price, a UI move, infrastructure code). notable = everything in between.
